content.text: The 1930s reshaped logic. **Kurt Gödel** found the limits of formal proof. **Alfred Tarski** defined truth for formal languages. **Gerhard Gentzen** analyzed the structure of proofs. **Alan Turing** defined computation.

examples.title: The halting problem
lines: Turing showed that no program can decide, for every program and input, whether it will halt.
examples.note: Some well defined questions have no algorithm at all.

options: A proof that logic is complete
question.hint: He worked on what it means for a sentence to be true.
question.explanation: Tarski gave the first rigorous definition of truth for a formal language, the foundation of model theory.
